text:
A low-carbohydrate intake depletes glycogen stores and shifts metabolism toward fat oxidation and ketogenesis, which can impair high-intensity exercise performance while being used therapeutically for weight loss and glycemic control. Effects vary with the degree of restriction, duration, and individual activity level. Because high-intensity exercise depends on rapid glycolytic ATP production from carbohydrate, performance suffers when carbohydrate availability is low.
CONFIDENCE: 78
